title: A permeability assay for mouse intestinal organoids
author: den Daas, Soffientini, et al.

steps.title: Plate organoids in Matrigel
steps.instruction: Embed organoids in a 30 µL Matrigel dome per well of a 24‑well plate, add 500 µL pre‑warmed growth medium, and aim for ~50–100 organoids per dome to avoid overlap; scale volumes as needed.

steps.title: Stain organoids with PI (optional Hoechst)
steps.instruction: Prepare staining solution and incubate organoids.

substeps.instruction: Dilute PI stock (5 mg/mL) in pre‑warmed organoid growth medium to a final concentration of 5 µg/mL (PI is added to growth medium, not PBS, to maintain organoid health).
Replace the existing medium in each well with the PI‑containing medium and incubate at 37 °C for 20 min.

Optional: add Hoechst (5 mg/mL stock) to the same medium to reach a final concentration of 5 µg/mL. Hoechst is toxic after prolonged exposure (>12 h) and is not recommended for permeability measurements longer than 12 h.

steps.title: Baseline imaging of organoids
steps.instruction: Acquire a Z‑stack of each well in the required fluorescence channels.

substeps.instruction: Place the plate in a Cytation 5 (or any automated fluorescent microscope capable of repeat imaging on the same x‑y‑z axis, e.g., ImageXpress Nano; note that alternative systems require protocol optimization).
Image a Z‑stack at 4× magnification in the green channel (469–525 nm) and red channel (531–593 nm).
If Hoechst staining was performed, also acquire the blue channel (377–447 nm).
Optional: acquire bright‑field images.

steps.title: Add treatments and collect LDH sample
steps.instruction: Introduce test compounds and controls, then sample medium for LDH assay.

substeps.instruction: Add the test toxin/compound(s) to the appropriate wells.
Add negative control medium to control wells.
Add EDTA to designated wells to a final concentration of 2 mM (positive permeable control).
Add Triton X‑100 to designated wells to a final concentration of 0.5 % (positive cell‑death control).
Immediately collect 2 µL of supernatant from each well for a lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) assay before the next imaging step.

steps.title: Post‑treatment imaging
steps.instruction: Re‑image the same fields after treatment.

substeps.instruction: Return the plate to the Cytation 5 (or the same microscope used for baseline imaging).
Image the same positions in the same fluorescence channels as before.
For EDTA and Triton X‑100 controls, acquire images after 150 min; for other compounds, adjust the incubation time as needed based on their mode of action.

steps.title: Measure LDH release
steps.instruction: Quantify cell death using the collected supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Perform the LDH assay on the 2 µL samples according to the kit instructions to determine membrane damage.
Optional: use an alternative validated cell‑death assay (requires optimization for 3D organoids).

steps.title: Define organoid lumen in green channel
steps.instruction: Create a region of interest (ROI) that corresponds to the lumen using the green‑channel image at time point 0.

substeps.instruction: Open the green‑channel Z‑stack of time point 0 in Fiji.
Z‑project the stack (Image → Stacks → Z Project…, Max Intensity).
Set an appropriate Threshold (Image → Adjust → Threshold) so that only the green background autofluorescence of lumen debris is selected.
Create a selection from the binary image (Edit → Selection → Create Selection).

steps.title: Measure PI intensity in lumen (time 0)
steps.instruction: Quantify baseline PI fluorescence within the lumen ROI.

substeps.instruction: Open the red‑channel Z‑stack of time point 0 in Fiji.
Z‑project the stack (Max Intensity).
Paste the previously created lumen selection (Ctrl + Shift + E).
Measure the mean intensity (Analyze → Measure).

steps.title: Measure PI intensity for later time points
steps.instruction: Repeat PI quantification for each subsequent time point using the same ROI.

substeps.instruction: Open the red‑channel Z‑stack for the desired time point.
Z‑project (Max Intensity).
Paste the lumen selection (Ctrl + Shift + E).
Measure mean PI intensity (Analyze → Measure).

steps.title: Statistical comparison of permeability
steps.instruction: Analyze differences in PI intensity between treated and control organoids.

substeps.instruction: Compare mean PI intensities of treated organoids to those of untreated controls using an appropriate statistical test (e.g., t‑test, ANOVA).
Optional: calculate the ratio of post‑treatment PI intensity to the time‑point 0 intensity for each organoid as an alternative metric.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps to measure permeability of intestinal organoids derived from mouse intestines, however this protocol could also be used to measure permeability intestinal organoids derived from other species. Intestinal organoid derival and culture needs to be set up prior to initiating this protocol. This permeability assay rapidly measures the permeability of live organoids in a matter of hours. Therefore, the intestinal organoids need to be plated and grown prior to the assay according to the researchers’ requirements, i.e., at least one day to analyze the effect of a substance on permeability of growing intestinal organoids, or 3–6 days on fully grown intestinal organoids. Plated intestinal organoids should be at a density to allow individual organoid imaging without overlapping organoids to simplify imaging analysis (∼50–100 organoids per dome). We plate a single 30 μL Matrigel dome with intestinal organoids in a 24-wells plate with 500 μL medium to measure permeability, but this can be scaled up or down depending on experimental requirements. Additional wells with organoids in the experiment can be used as a negative control, positive permeabilized control (e.g., ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, EDTA), and positive cell death control (e.g., Triton X-100).
